subject: Audit logs & data access evidence request - FincoBank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Patel <jason.patel@fincobank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit logs & data access evidence request - FincoBank

Hi Jason —

Thanks again for taking the time on the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on what FincoBank needs and what Redwood can provide:

What you asked for (recap):
- Export of audit logs showing data access (who accessed what and when) for the last 90 days.
- Fields: timestamp (ISO8601), resource (model/endpoint/dataset), user_id (or hashed id), action (query/read/export), request_id, ip_address, region, model_version, token_count.
- Clarification on what PII is present in logs and any redaction applied.
- Preferred format: CSV (spreadsheet), with optional JSONL for system ingestion.
- A short statement describing retention windows and availability of per-user/export evidence for procurement.

Our ask / timeline:
- Can you share a sample 1-2MB extract (CSV) covering ~7 days from the last 90-day window so our security and procurement teams can validate format and fields?
- Procurement is aiming to finalize evidence by 2026-03-15. If you can send the sample by end of day Friday (3/12), that would keep us on track.

Notes on Redwood capability (high-level):
- Redwood can export audit logs in CSV or JSONL. Exports include the fields listed above.
- Default platform retention for audit logs is configurable under Dedicated/Enterprise contracts; we can provide extracts for arbitrary retention windows within your contract limits.
- We do not store raw PII in request bodies; user identifiers in logs are typically hashed or tenant-scoped IDs. We can provide guidance on redaction if you need fields removed before sharing.

Attachments: if you prefer, you can attach the sample as fincobank_audit_extract_sample.csv (small extract).

Next steps:
- Jason to send sample extract (CSV) + short note on redaction/PII by 3/12 EOD.
- Marissa to confirm Redwood export schema and give ETA for a full 90-day export once sample validated.
- Loop Ben for a quick engineering confirmation on export process/ETA.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jason Patel <jason.patel@fincobank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access evidence request - FincoBank

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We can pull a 7-day extract and will scrub any direct email addresses before sending. I’m attaching a small sample (fincobank_audit_extract_sample.csv) that contains the fields we currently capture. A couple quick questions where we’d appreciate clarification so the sample is useful for your team:

1) Export format: we can produce CSV and JSONL. Any preference from Redwood for which to send first?
2) Retention: we currently retain full access logs for 180 days in our systems; is that sufficient for Redwood’s evaluation or do you need evidence beyond 180 days?

I’ll attach the small CSV in my next message (we’ll redact any PII). If possible, confirm the exact column headings you expect so we can align format.

Thanks,
Jason Patel
Head of IT Security — FincoBank
jason.patel@fincobank.com

Attachment: fincobank_audit_extract_sample.csv (CSV, ~400KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jason Patel <jason.patel@fincobank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access evidence request - FincoBank

Jason —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. CSV is perfect for the initial review; JSONL is great for ingestion later. To be explicit, the column headings we expect are:
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- user_id (hashed or tenant-scoped id)
- resource (model_name or endpoint)
- action (query/read/export)
- request_id
- ip_address
- region
- model_version
- token_count

A few clarifications from our side:
- Redwood does not persist raw request bodies that contain PII. Audit logs contain metadata (including hashed user ids or tenant-specific identifiers) and request metadata (IP, region, model_version).
- Default retention on our hosted plans is 365 days; for Dedicated/Enterprise plans retention is contract-configurable. If FincoBank needs a retention certificate or statement, we can provide a short attestation describing retention and deletion procedures.
- For procurement, a 7-day CSV sample is fine for format validation. Once we validate the sample, we’ll request a full 90-day extract. We can accept CSV or JSONL for the 90-day export.

I’m attaching our internal audit playbook (redwood_audit_playbook.pdf) which outlines our export format and common redaction practices — this may help your team map fields. Ben — can you confirm the expected ETA to produce a 90-day export if the sample looks good?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_audit_playbook.pdf (PDF, ~120KB)

timestamp,user_id,resource,action,request_id,ip_address,region,model_version,token_count

If you need a signed attestation on retention/availability or SOC2 excerpt, let me know and I’ll coordinate with compliance.
